content:
If you are a large app user using the Apple Watch beta this summer, you may have noticed that some existing apps cannot launch on watchOS 27. Apple has identified this issue and is automatically updating apps on behalf of developers to ensure compatibility.

This update is pushed via the App Store, and the update notes read: "This app has been updated by Apple to prepare for compatibility with watchOS 27. No new features are included."

Apple has notified developers this week that this process will be completed by August 31.

watchOS 27 (along with iOS 27 and other new operating systems) is expected to be released to the public around mid-September, so the related updates have been pushed out early enough.

Apple stated that because some watchOS apps' arm64 encoding has issues, this handling is required. It appears they are automatically reprocessing and repackaging apps to fix binary compatibility issues, allowing existing apps to continue to function without developers needing to take any action.
